STEP 1 - Scene: A small pile of soft white cubed/chunked cheese (looks like fresh mozzarella or paneer-style cheese, lightly textured) on a white square plate. Photographed from a high, near-overhead angle.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white square plate is roughly 20 cm across (side plate size). Its width spans about 330 px in the image, and the cheese pile is about a third of that span. Vessel area ≈ 20 × 20 × ~0.85 (rounded corners) ≈ 340 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: One food: white cheese pieces (mozzarella/paneer-like), roughly 15–20 chunks, each about 2–3 cm.

STEP 4 - Area: The cheese covers about 20% of the plate's area (pile spans roughly 2/3 of the plate's width but is concentrated in the middle). Cheese ≈ 20% of 340 cm² ≈ 68 cm².

STEP 5 - Volume: Typical pile height ~1.5 cm (chunks stacked, some up to 2.5 cm). 68 cm² × 1.5 cm ≈ 100 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Cheese bulk density ~0.95 g/ml → 100 ml × 0.95 ≈ 95 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Fresh mozzarella/paneer-type cheese ≈ 280–300 kcal/100 g. Use 290 kcal/100 g → 95 g × 2.9 ≈ 275 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A ~95 g portion of soft white cheese on a small plate is plausible for a modest serving; roughly 275 kcal fits what is visible.
